function_v0.doc:
Deliver one output; return its stored `keccak256(solver || timestamp:u32)` record.

`filler` authorizes the invocation and must approve this contract to pull the
context-priced amount. `solver` is the nonzero origin claimant ID, independent
of the payer. `output` is the full mandate; its context's recipient tag derives
the native recipient.
`fill_deadline` is an inclusive Unix-second limit and must be the origin order's
committed deadline: the record lives only until `fill_deadline + NOT_FILLED_WINDOW`,
so an understated deadline lets anyone mint a valid non-fill once it lapses.

# Effects
New fills transfer to the recipient, store the record in temporary storage
extended to the fill horizon, and emit `OutputFilled`. Existing fills return the
old record without payment or another event, after all validation; retries extend
the record to this call's horizon (never shortening it). Any failure rolls
everything back.

# Errors
Wrong domain, unsupported callback, invalid or exclusive context,
zero solver, arithmet
function_v0.name: fill

event_v0.doc:
A new fill record was written and paid. `payload` is the canonical fill
description (solver, order, timestamp and common payload); together with the
emitter's immutable configuration it reconstructs the complete mandate.
`final_amount` is the amount actually transferred after context pricing.
event_v0.name: OutputFilled

instance/code TTL. Permissionless. `Malformed` for a partial tuple; `Unproven` if any
tuple is absent or expired (an expired proof is re-created by `set_attestation`
while its fill record lives). A failure rolls back every renewal.

function_v0.doc:
Return whether every payload has a matching fill record or a valid non-fill.

`oracle` is an explicit raw namespace: export adapters must pass their own contract
ID and authenticate the remote chain/application. Accepts 0\xe2\x80\x934 exact canonical
payloads of at most 684 bytes; an empty query returns `true`. Fill proofs compare
stored solver/timestamp; non-fills require no fill and
`committed deadline < now <= committed deadline + NOT_FILLED_WINDOW`. Outside that
window a non-fill is `false`: the fill record may have expired.

Oversized callback/context fields within a bounded proof are answered truthfully:
no such fill can exist, while non-fill follows the deadline. This differs from
`fill`/`emit_not_filled` admission. No authorization or data TTL renewal occurs;
instance/code TTL is maintained. Malformed proofs, unknown proof prefixes, or bounds errors
abort rather than returning `false`.
function_v0.name: has_attested

function_v0.doc:
Bind the immutable OIF destination `chain_id` and expected Stellar `network_id`.

Returns `WrongNetwork` if the network differs from the host ledger. Stores
configuration in instance storage and renews instance/code TTL. There is no
administrator or mutable deployment configuration.
function_v0.name: __constructor

function_v0.doc:
Emit and return a canonical non-fill proof when
`fill_deadline < now <= fill_deadline + NOT_FILLED_WINDOW` and unfilled.

Permissionless. Validates chain, settler and output byte bounds; it does not execute
or validate callback/context semantics. Emits `OutputNotFilled`, storing no marker.
An early caller-supplied deadline cannot block fills. Consumers must reconstruct
the proof using their committed deadline; a recorded fill even after that deadline
blocks emission. Maintains instance/code TTL, not fill TTL.

# Errors
`DeadlineNotPassed`, `NotFilledWindowElapsed`, `AlreadyFilled`,
domain/configuration or resource-bound errors.
function_v0.name: emit_not_filled

function_v0.doc:
Read the record for `order_id` and `keccak256(full packed MandateOutput)`.

Returns `None` for an unknown pair, and once the temporary record has expired after
`fill_deadline + NOT_FILLED_WINDOW`; a known record commits solver and timestamp.
Permissionless; maintains instance/code TTL but not fill TTL. Configuration
errors abort.
function_v0.name: get_fill_record

function_v0.doc:
Record a local input-oracle proof for an existing fill of `output`.

Permissionless, as on EVM `setAttestation`. `output.oracle` must be this settler.
The stored fill record must equal `keccak256(solver || timestamp:u32)`; the proof
is then `keccak(proof_tuple(output, keccak(fill payload)))`, a temporary entry
living `TTL_TARGET` ledgers. Repeat calls are idempotent and restore the full
proof TTL, re-creating an expired proof while the fill record lives. No event is
emitted: `OutputFilled` already carries the payload. Only fills are attestable;
unfilled same-chain orders refund through the escrow's `refund` after `expires`.

# Errors
`WrongChain`, `WrongSettler`, `ResourceLimit`, `WrongOracle`, `InvalidAttestation`,
`WireLimit` or configuration errors.
function_v0.name: set_attestation

function_v0.doc:
Decode the native destination a fill of `output` would pay.

Applies the fill's chain, settler, byte-bound, callback and context-shape rules.
The result is a G, C or M address according to the context's recipient tag. It
does not predict token, trustline, pricing-time or authorization outcomes.

# Errors
`WrongChain`, `WrongSettler`, `ResourceLimit`, `CallbackUnsupported`,
`InvalidContext`, or configuration errors.
function_v0.name: resolve_recipient

function_v0.doc:
Atomically fill 1\xe2\x80\x934 outputs of this settler for one order with the same filler and proposed solver.

The filler authorizes this call and grants token allowances as for `fill`.
The first output's record must equal this call's `keccak256(solver || now:u32)`:
a previous fill even by the same solver at another second loses competition.
Later filled outputs skip payment after validation. New outputs emit `OutputFilled`;
all writes/transfers roll back on failure. Fills and retries extend records to
the fill horizon, as for `fill`.

# Errors
`EmptyCollection`, `ResourceLimit`, `AlreadyFilled` for first-output competition,
or any domain, deadline, `FillHorizon`, context, token or authorization failure
from `fill`.
function_v0.name: fill_order_outputs

# Errors
`Malformed` for a partial 128-byte tuple, `Unproven` for any missing or expired proof.

udt_error_enum_v0.doc:
Settlement errors, codes 2000\xe2\x80\x932033, grouped by the phase that raises them.

Oracle adapters use 1000\xe2\x80\x931010 and the router adapter 3000\xe2\x80\x933009. All three ranges
avoid the Stellar Asset Contract's 1\xe2\x80\x9315 and the LI.FI router's codes below 1000:
nested failures propagate their callee's number, and a caller's typed client would
otherwise decode, say, a missing trustline as a settlement error.
udt_error_enum_v0.name: Error

udt_struct_v0.doc:
The shared cross-chain output, field for field the reference `MandateOutput`.
Every field is a wire identifier, so `token`, `settler` and `oracle` are raw
32-byte IDs and `recipient` is a raw 32-byte payload rather than a native
`Address`: the output may live on any chain and is hashed into proofs as-is.
`amount` is the original mandate amount; Dutch pricing never changes it.
udt_struct_v0.name: MandateOutput

fields.doc: Original unsigned destination base-unit amount; context pricing does not alter the commitment.
fields.name: amount

fields.doc: Opaque destination callback bytes, at most 256; Stellar fills require empty bytes.

fields.name: chain_id

fields.doc: Opaque fulfillment context, at most 256 bytes; local execution uses supported exact layouts.
fields.name: context

fields.doc: Raw output-oracle ID; the source adapter must attest in this exact namespace.
fields.name: oracle

fields.doc: Destination recipient identifier; Stellar uses the raw G key or C ID typed by the context tag.
